hints.title: Pair Parity Disruption Obstacle
hints.text: Every element appears twice except one, and the entire array is sorted. How does the index parity of identical pairs change before and after the single element?

hints.title: Even-Odd Parity Invariant
hints.text: Before the unique element, pairs begin at even indices (even, odd). After the unique element, pairs are shifted to (odd, even).

hints.title: Even Index Bisection Procedure
hints.text: Set left = 0, right = len(nums) - 1. While left < right, compute mid = (left + right) // 2. Ensure mid is even by subtracting 1 if mid % 2 == 1. If nums[mid] == nums[mid + 1], the disruption lies strictly to the right (left = mid + 2); otherwise it is at or to the left (right = mid). Return nums[left].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Logarithmic bisection checking index parity of paired occurrences in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Linear XOR reduction takes O(N) which misses the logarithmic bound achievable on sorted arrays.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using bitwise mid ^ 1 or parity alignment to compare adjacent partners in O(1) checks.
